You'll understand how to use pretrained large language models for use cases like copywriting and summarization; create semantic search systems that go beyond keyword matching; and use existing libraries and pretrained models for text classification, search, and clusterings.

issue_title: Dear Architects
title: Deciphering Data Architectures
description: Data fabric, data lakehouse, and data mesh have recently appeared as viable alternatives to the modern data warehouse. These new architectures have solid benefits, but they're also surrounded by a lot of hyperbole and confusion. This practical book provides a guided tour of these architectures to help data professionals understand the pros and cons of each.

issue_title: Dear Architects
title: Platform Strategy
description: Harvested from a decade of building successful in-house platforms and enabling enterprises to utilize cloud platforms, this book provides a fresh look at what makes IT platforms work, why they are different from other IT services, and how you can use them to boost developer productivity. Sticky metaphors (“are you building a fruit salad or fruit basket?"; “build abstractions not illusions!”) provide actionable design guidance without being lecturing or boring.

issue_title: Dear Architects
title: Learning Domain-Driven Design
description: Building software is harder than ever. As a developer, you not only have to chase ever-changing technological trends but also need to understand the business domains behind the software. This practical book provides you with a set of core patterns, principles, and practices for analyzing business domains, understanding business strategy, and, most importantly, aligning software design with its business needs.

issue_title: Dear Architects
title: Unbreakable AWS Data Protection Starts Here!
description: Rubrik's AWS Native Protection empowers businesses to secure critical cloud infrastructure like Amazon Aurora, S3, EC2, and RDS, offering centralized, automated protection against cyber threats while ensuring data remains readily available and recoverable across multi-cloud environments. Discover how to safeguard your cloud data today.

issue_title: Dear Architects
title: Engineering Resilient Systems on AWS
description: To ensure that applications are reliable and always available, more businesses today are moving applications to AWS. But many companies still struggle to design and build these cloud applications effectively, thinking that because the cloud is resilient, their applications will be too. With this practical guide, software, DevOps, and cloud engineers will learn how to implement resilient designs and configurations in the cloud using hands-on independent labs.

issue_title: Dear Architects
title: Prompt Engineering for Generative AI
description: Large language models (LLMs) and diffusion models such as ChatGPT and Stable Diffusion have unprecedented potential. Because they have been trained on all the public text and images on the internet, they can make useful contributions to a wide variety of tasks. And with the barrier to entry greatly reduced today, practically any developer can harness LLMs and diffusion models to tackle problems previously unsuitable for automation.

issue_title: Dear Architects
title: RAG-Driven Generative AI
description: This book offers a detailed exploration of RAG and how to design, manage, and control multimodal AI pipelines. By connecting outputs to traceable source documents, RAG improves output accuracy and contextual relevance, offering a dynamic approach to managing large volumes of information. This AI book shows you how to build a RAG framework, providing practical knowledge on vector stores, chunking, indexing, and ranking.

issue_title: Dear Architects
title: Architecture Modernization
description: Concrete tools, techniques, and processes to align software architecture with your business domains, organizational design, team topologies, and corporate strategy. Written for anyone who makes decisions about software architecture or organization design, including architects, CTOs, principal engineers, and tech leads.

issue_title: Dear Architects
title: Communication Patterns
description: Misunderstanding and lack of buy-in leads to increasing costs, unmet requirements, and an architecture that is not what you intended. Through constructive examples and patterns, this book shows you how to create documentation and diagrams that actually get the message across to the different audiences you'll face.

issue_title: Dear Architects
title: Balancing Coupling in Software Design

issue_title: Dear Architects
title: Facilitating Software Architecture
description: The software architect role is evolving. As systems and their interactions with the teams that build, run, and evolve them become more complex, it's often impossible for those playing the traditional architect roles to be everywhere they need to be. There's simply too much architecture to be done, and the situation has reached a breaking point.

issue_title: Dear Architects
title: AI Engineering

issue_title: #305 - Architecture as a craft, data for agents, and the end of programming
title: Architecture as a Socio-Technical Craft
author: Luca Mezzalira
description: Architecture is not merely a set of diagrams or abstract patterns; it is a socio-technical craft where technical decisions intersect with organizational dynamics, cognitive load, and team topologies.

issue_title: #305 - Architecture as a craft, data for agents, and the end of programming
title: Why Agent Memory is a Database Problem
author: Oracle Research
description: LLMs are getting better at reasoning, reducing the need for prompt and context engineering. The focus is now on making agents adaptable to new information and long-horizon tasks, where simply adding a vector store falls short. Instead, agents need a memory substrate that manages working, factual, and procedural states natively within the database.

issue_title: #305 - Architecture as a craft, data for agents, and the end of programming
title: You can't govern what you can't see
author: Luca Mezzalira
description: Structure would have told you something changed, but not what it meant. That service's dependency graph grew an edge. It is a fact, and whether it is a defect depends entirely on what you were trying to build, which no dependency tool knows. A rising coupling number on a service that is deliberately becoming a hub is progress; the same number on one that was meant to stay isolated is rot.

issue_title: #305 - Architecture as a craft, data for agents, and the end of programming
title: Making Your Data Ready for Agentic AI
author: Martin Fowler
description: Agentic systems can only act well on data they can actually find, interpret and trust. Preparing data for agents means investing in context, quality and clear semantics before adding more model capability.

issue_title: #305 - Architecture as a craft, data for agents, and the end of programming
title: The end of programming
author: Paul Dix
description: The craft of writing code by hand is being replaced by directing systems that write code for us. What matters now is judgement about what to build, how to verify it, and where the real constraints live.

issue_title: #305 - Architecture as a craft, data for agents, and the end of programming
title: Running a Software Factory Efficiently at Uber Scale
author: Uber Engineering
description: Running a software factory at Uber scale means treating build, test and deployment infrastructure as a product with its own reliability and efficiency targets. Small inefficiencies in the developer workflow multiply across thousands of engineers.
